2. Compare with solarlytics-backend/.github/workflows/ci.yml and solarlytics-frontend/.github/workflows/ci.yml.
3. Read HANDOFF.md section 2 ("How changes come in": branch, pull request, the owner merges) and section 8.C (DEP-01 not built).

label: feature-gap
steps:
1. `ls gridlytics-backend`: there is no Dockerfile, .dockerignore, .env.production.example or docs/DEPLOY.md.
2. Collect the GRIDLYTICS_* names the package reads (`grep -ohE 'GRIDLYTICS_[A-Z0-9_]+' backend/gridlytics/*.py | sort -u`, 31 names) and the names the Markdown docs and .env.example mention in both repositories, then diff the two lists.
3. `curl -si http://127.0.0.1:8151/api/health | grep -i server`.
4. Compare with solarlytics-backend's Dockerfile, .dockerignore, .env.production.example and docs/DEPLOY.md, and with boxlytics-backend's backend/Dockerfile, deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml, nginx-boxlytics-backend.conf and boxlytics-backend.service.
actual: None of these files exist. The only settings documented anywhere are GRIDLYTICS_SCHEDULER, DATA_DIR, DEMO_DAYS and DEMO_REPLAN_HOURS. Undocumented: AUTH_MODE, HOSTS, CORS_ORIGINS, CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX, LOCAL_JWT_SECRET, TRUST_PROXY, the founder four, the Supabase five, JWKS_TTL, MEMBERSHIP_TTL, JWT_AUDIENCE, the three RATE_* limits, DAILY_BACKUP, RESET_BACKUP, LOGS, DOCS, DB and WEB_DIST. A hosted start with GRIDLYTICS_HOSTS set and no LOCAL_JWT_SECRET is refused by identity.check_startup, and no document says why. The live API sends `server: uvicorn`. No backend host is chosen anywhere in the repositories.
evidence: Undocumented-settings diff: 27 of 31. curl /api/health response headers include `server: uvicorn`. backend/gridlytics/identity.py:116-136 (check_startup). solarlytics-backend/Dockerfile (uid 10001, VOLUME /data, HEALTHCHECK, --proxy-headers --no-server-header), solarlytics-backend/.env.production.example, solarlytics-backend/docs/DEPLOY.md, solarlytics-backend/backend/tests/test_deploy_docs.py. HANDOFF 8.C lists DEP-04, DEP-06 and DEP-07 as not built.

title: env.ts throws away every build setting when one is invalid: VITE_AUTH_MODE=supabase, which the backend accepts, silently resets VITE_API_BASE_URL to '' so a hosted page calls /api on its own host
label: bug
steps:
1. Build the web app with VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://api.example.pk/api and VITE_AUTH_MODE=supabase. The server side accepts GRIDLYTICS_AUTH_MODE=supabase (identity.py:126).
2. Or run the same zod schema in node from frontend/: Env.safeParse({VITE_API_BASE_URL:'https://api.example.pk/api', VITE_AUTH_MODE:'supabase'}).
3. Look at API_BASE and AUTH_MODE.
expected: An invalid or unsupported setting stops the build with a sentence (Solarlytics' deploy_check.mjs refuses an unset or unknown VITE_AUTH_MODE). A valid VITE_API_BASE_URL is never discarded because a different variable failed. The backend and the web app agree on which sign-in modes exist: either the web app gains supabase mode, or the backend's supabase mode is documented as not usable with this web app.
actual: safeParse fails on the enum, and env.ts falls back to the whole default object {VITE_API_BASE_URL:'', VITE_AUTH_MODE:'local'}, so API_BASE becomes '/api'. A Vercel build pointed at the API host would call its own origin (404 on Vercel) and post to /api/local/session, a route a supabase-mode server never mounts (api.py mounts routes_local only in local mode). Nothing warns.
evidence: frontend/src/app/env.ts:7-17: `VITE_AUTH_MODE: z.enum(["local"])` and `export const env = parsed.success ? parsed.data : { VITE_API_BASE_URL: "", VITE_AUTH_MODE: "local" as const }`. Node reproduction with the repository's zod: `false {"VITE_API_BASE_URL":"","VITE_AUTH_MODE":"local"} API_BASE= /api`. backend api.py:530-532 (routes_local mounted only when identity.MODE == 'local'). solarlytics-frontend/frontend/scripts/deploy_check.mjs envProblems().

title: Every scratch run writes its log into the owner's data folder: api.py logs beside GRIDLYTICS_DB's default (gridlytics-backend/data/logs), and the launcher's --scratch sets only GRIDLYTICS_DATA_DIR
label: bug
steps:
1. Start the scratch app: `python scripts/start_local.py --scratch` in gridlytics-frontend, as HANDOFF section 3 says.
2. Check the API process: `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/<uvicorn pid>/environ | grep -E '^GRIDLYTICS_(DB|DATA_DIR)='` and `ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd | grep gridlytics-backend/data`.
3. `ls -la gridlytics-backend/data/logs/` and `ls gridlytics-backend/.scratch/data` (there is no logs/ folder there).
expected:
A scratch run writes nothing under gridlytics-backend/data (HANDOFF section 7: "Never delete, reseed or write test data into gridlytics-backend/data"). Its log goes to <scratch folder>/logs. Two ways to fix it, and both are worth doing:
- api.py logs to platformdb.data_dir()/'logs' rather than store.DB_PATH.parent/'logs';
- the launcher sets GRIDLYTICS_DB=<folder>/gridlytics.db together with GRIDLYTICS_DATA_DIR, as Solarlytics' launcher does (`env.update(SOLARLYTICS_DB=..., SOLARLYTICS_DATA_DIR=...)`).
A launcher test pins it. backups.daily_all should likewise not probe the default DB_PATH in the owner's folder.
actual: The scratch API (pid 183, port 8151) runs with GRIDLYTICS_DATA_DIR=.scratch/data and no GRIDLYTICS_DB. It holds gridlytics-backend/data/logs/gridlytics.log open. That file has 2,128 lines, was last written 9 Nov 12:26 by scratch requests, and holds the scratch run's 13 ERROR entries (7 tick failures, 6 unanswered requests). The scratch data folder has no logs/. Anyone debugging a scratch run must read the owner's folder, and the owner's real log gets mixed with test traffic.
evidence: backend/gridlytics/api.py:34-44 (`_logs = store.DB_PATH.parent / "logs"`); store.py:24 (DB_PATH defaults to <repo>/data/gridlytics.db); backups.py:87 (daily_all always includes Path(store.DB_PATH)). gridlytics-frontend/scripts/start_local.py:248-266 (only GRIDLYTICS_DATA_DIR set). solarlytics-frontend/scripts/start_local.py:231-236 (sets both SOLARLYTICS_DB and SOLARLYTICS_DATA_DIR). Process check: `GRIDLYTICS_DATA_DIR=/home/user/saad-tahir/gridlytics-backend/.scratch/data`, open fd `/home/user/saad-tahir/gridlytics-backend/data/logs/gridlytics.log`.
